text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Canada to fight Cuba law alone: European Union attempts to cut separate deal with U.S. to avoid trade battle.
- Bog at centre of N.S. furor: Ex-MLA's firms staked claims.
- Top North Korean may have defected: Seoul says official has sought asylum.
- Municipalities given say on downloading: Critics vocal on welfare cost-sharing plan.
- Cell phones set off car-accident alarm: Drivers' inattention quadruples risk of crash, U of T study finds.
- Fred Goldman persists in quest to obtain Simpson confession: Offer to exchange fine for admission of guilt rejected.
- Foreign bank rules to be eased: Ottawa set to allow branches to foster competition in small- and big-business lending.
- Fund crusader reported on the outs at OSC: Glorianne Stromberg losing her office, can't talk to staff, sources say.
- Swedish firm picks Toronto as base for mining unit: First TSE listing may total C$500-million.
- Martin playing to bondholders: If the market likes next week's budget, it'll be even more excited about Canada once the deficit is eliminated. Then there's the debt.
- Ottawa to probe Russian steel flood: Inquiry follows Stelco complaint that imports undercutting market.
- Talisman offers C$1.7 billion for Wascana Energy.
